The Model API allows you to view, create, delete and modify model elements in a project. This page will list best practices and dos and donts in using this API:
<p>
       * *Do not* use !EcoreUtil.delete() to delete model elements. Use project.delete() or modelElement.delete() to delete model elements.

    * *Do not* remove elements from the projects containment hierarchy. If you really want to remove the model elements, use delete operations in model element or project, otherwise move the element directly into its new containment: e.g. if a solution is contained in an issue, never call setIssue(null) in the solution. This would in effect remove the solution from the containment tree of the project. Instead add the solution directly in a new containment, e.g. project.addModelElement(solution) to add the solution to the project itself. Otherwise use project.delete() or modelElement.delete() as stated above.

    * *Do not* create a model element and add cross references before adding the element to the project. Create the element, add it to the project (either directly or somewhere in the containment tree) and only after that create cross references. The same is true if you add a containment tree of model elements, make sure neither of the elements has cross references, neither among each other nor to the outside of the tree. E.g. if you create a meeting and add meeting sections as containment. You may add the contained sections before adding meeting to the project but you may not add any other cross references (e.g. to action items) before doing so. You may alter simple attributes before adding model elements to the project containment tree.

    * *Intention Preservation:* Apply the changes on the model in the same way the user intended them in the user interface. E.g. the user opens a model element and clicks on "add comment": Add the comment to the model element by calling getComments().add(comment) on the model element. Do not call comment.setModelElement() on the comment. The way you modify the model reflects in the recorded operations.

    * *Composite Preservation:* If you perform several changes to the model that are triggered by only one intention (e.g. click) of the user, use the composite operation support in !ProjectSpace. You can call beginCompositeOperation() on the project space to announce a composite operation, you will receive a handle for the composite as a result (!CompositeOperationHandle). With the handle you can control the composite. Calling abort() on the handle will rollback the operation, this is usefull in dialogs where the user may cancel the changes at any time. Calling end() on the handle will complete the composite and preserve the changes.
</p>

   * *Commands:* To read from or change something in the model you need to run a command on the transactional editing domain the model is controlled by. Otherwise the editing domain will reject your read or your changes. This is necessary to synchronize different threads working on the model. You can use the code below to run a command on the model. There is also two additional Class for handling Parameters and return results with a command - UnicaseCommandWithResult and UnicaseCommandWithParameterAndResults.
{{{ 
new UnicaseCommand() {
   @Override 
      protected void doRun() {
        //your code in here
      }
   }.run(); 
}}}
